reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a coordinated dance tutorial rather than a financial or data-collection solicitation. Its Instagram, class, and email references are described as ordinary promotional or contact information, with no connection to deceptive promises or required financial participation.

opening.argument: The video directs viewers toward an external participation pathway: it provides an Instagram account, a class link, and a direct email contact. Although the promised benefit is framed as instruction, the viewer is still being asked to leave the video and contact or follow the promoter to obtain it. That action-linked promotion is enough to warrant treating the content as a solicitation rather than assuming the offer is benign. The dance performance supplies attention and credibility, while the off-platform route supplies the conversion mechanism.

citations.quote: Follow me on Instagram: http://instagram.com/deepaktulsyan for Classes: https://goo.gl/vBqDCz Contact - [EMAIL]

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not resolve the solicitation issue. The description explicitly pairs following an Instagram account with obtaining classes and also supplies a shortened external link and an email address. The reference argument assumes these are merely ordinary contact details, but it does not establish that viewers receive the advertised classes without taking those off-platform actions.

citations.quote: Follow me on Instagram: http://instagram.com/deepaktulsyan for Classes: https://goo.gl/vBqDCz Contact - [EMAIL]

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited description shows only that classes are promoted and contact information is available; it does not promise a free reward, income, withdrawal, or unusually easy acquisition. It also does not show that following Instagram, clicking the link, or emailing is required, paid, or deceptive. The title and frames support an instructional dance presentation, not a fraudulent acquisition scheme.

opening.argument: Several external-contact signals appear together: a social-media handle, a shortened URL, an email address, and a stated route to classes. That combination moves the viewer from a polished demonstration into an off-platform funnel whose terms, costs, and delivery are not shown in the video. The absence of those details matters because the audience is encouraged to pursue the offer without being given transparent conditions. A careful reviewer should therefore treat the easy transition from watching to contacting as a meaningful risk signal.

citations.quote: Follow me on Instagram: http://instagram.com/deepaktulsyan for Classes: https://goo.gl/vBqDCz Contact - [EMAIL]

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side describes the links as ordinary promotion, but that is precisely the unsupported assumption at issue. The description contains multiple routes away from the platform while omitting any visible price, terms, or explanation of what the class link provides. The coordinated performance may attract viewers, yet it does not make the external funnel transparent or trustworthy.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External links and contact details are not themselves evidence of a scam. The supplied material contains no reward, return, payment demand, credential request, or claim of effortless acquisition. The frames show a coordinated dance demonstration, while the description identifies the external destination as classes; missing pricing or terms does not establish deception.

opening.argument: The apparent educational role also functions as direct promotion. The title presents a running-man tutorial, and the frames show a lead dancer demonstrating movements with two accompanying dancers; alongside that instruction, the description tells viewers to follow an account for classes and supplies a link and email contact. Thus the lesson is not merely information: it is the promotional front end for a viewer-action pathway. The instructional framing can make that solicitation seem more trustworthy than a plainly commercial appeal.

citations.quote: Follow me on Instagram: http://instagram.com/deepaktulsyan for Classes: https://goo.gl/vBqDCz Contact - [EMAIL]

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side focuses on the choreography but does not address the explicit commercial direction attached to it. The description does not merely identify the performer; it tells viewers to follow the account for classes and provides two contact routes. The tutorial format can therefore be understood as the persuasive vehicle that drives viewers toward the external offer.

citations.quote: Follow me on Instagram: http://instagram.com/deepaktulsyan for Classes: https://goo.gl/vBqDCz Contact - [EMAIL]

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of dance classes is consistent with ordinary educational content and does not show a fraudulent reward or acquisition claim. The title accurately identifies a tutorial, and the frames show the stated dance instruction. The description's phrase “for Classes” identifies the subject of the link, but does not show that viewers are misled, required to pay, or promised an easy reward.
